citations.evidenceText:
Uncertainty in Robotics

•   Classical robots in a highly engineered environments (industrial assembly) are
   studied as a deterministic system (precisely known link lengths & joint angles).
•  However, this determinism collapses in an unstructured “open world” (outdoor)
   environment due to enormous uncertainty inherent in the physical world:
   – Environment: Dynamic & unpredictable, especially near humans.
   – Sensors: Limited range/resolution, noisy measurements, and possible failures.
   – Actuators: Motors control noise, wear-and-tear and mechanical failures.
   – Model Errors: Mathematical models only approximate
       real-world physics.
   – Algorithmic Approximations: Faster algorithms trade
       accuracy for computational efficiency.
